title: Synchronous service calls
idea: A synchronous call is one service sending an HTTP request to another and waiting for the answer. The caller shares that service's speed and failures.
points: The caller's response time includes every call it waits on.
While waiting, each request holds a connection and memory.
A timeout caps the wait; without one, a slow service stalls its callers.
Retry only requests that are safe to repeat, with growing delays between tries.

steps.caption: Orders needs stock data, so it sends an HTTP request to Inventory and waits for the reply.
Healthy case: Inventory answers, then Orders answers the client. The client waits for both calls.
Inventory slows down. Orders keeps waiting, and each waiting request holds a connection and memory.
With no timeout, waiting requests pile up in Orders faster than they finish.
Orders runs out of connections or memory, so even requests that never touch Inventory fail. That is a cascading failure.
Fix one: set a timeout. Orders gives up after a short wait, frees the request and returns an error fast.
Fix two: retry only brief glitches, with growing delays. Instant retries add load to a service that is already struggling.

code.title: Timeout and retry
code.caption: A stand-in Inventory service hangs on its first call. The caller times out, waits and retries.

walk.text: A stand-in Inventory service. Its first call never replies; later calls do.
Listen on a free port and build the URL.
`AbortSignal.timeout(200)` aborts the request after 200 ms, so `fetch` rejects.
On success, print the reply and stop retrying.
A timeout lands here as a `TimeoutError`.
Wait longer after each failure, so a struggling service gets room to recover.
Shut the server down so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Set a timeout on every outgoing call; a missing one lets a hung service hang you.
Do not retry instantly or in unlimited loops; retry storms overload a struggling service.
Do not retry a POST that changes data unless repeating it is safe.

quiz.q: The first call hangs and the second answers. What does the script print?
options: attempt 1 TimeoutError, then attempt 2 in stock
attempt 1 TimeoutError, attempt 2 TimeoutError, attempt 3 TimeoutError
quiz.why: The 200 ms timeout aborts the hung call and `fetch` rejects with `TimeoutError`. The loop waits, retries, and the second call succeeds.

takeaway: Every synchronous call needs a timeout, and every retry needs a limit.
